subject: Request: Tiered SLA exception for p95 spike on model omega-v2
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@fintrade.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected p95 increase — request for temporary tiered SLA exception for model omega-v2

Alex / team —

We are seeing a sustained p95 latency increase for model 'omega-v2' serving FinTrade traffic in us-east-1 over the last ~3 hours. Summary:
- Baseline p95: ~240ms (last 30d)
- Current p95: 920–1,050ms (rolling 15m)
- Error-rate: unchanged; throughput steady; tail appears correlated with longer sequences for a small subset of requests.

Immediate impact: increased client-side latency and timeouts for real-time quoting flows. We suspect a combination of a recent runtime kernel selection change + a quantization schedule that affected long-context fanouts for this variant. Our on-call has traced higher KV-cache misses on those sessions (attached: p95_trend.png, prod-logs-snippet.txt).

Request: We propose a temporary, tiered SLA exception for FinTrade's production traffic to allow the following mitigations without triggering automatic incident rollback/penalties:
1) 6-hour provisional exception window starting now to allow diagnostics and a controlled canary rollback if needed.
2) If p95 remains >=700ms after 45 minutes, we'll proceed with a canary rollback to omega-v1.7 for 10% of traffic, expanding by 25% every 15 minutes if improvement observed.
3) We'll apply a KV-cache aggressiveness bump and pin long-sequence workloads to the dedicated pool during the window.

We need two approvals to proceed: FinTrade authorization for the SLA carveout, and internal product ops sign-off to execute the rollback. Ben / Kimberly — can you approve the operational plan below so I can share it with Alex?

Planned step-by-step (high level):
- 09:45 PT: increase KV-cache TTL for session keys + switch long-sequence flagging
- 10:00 PT: evaluate 15m p95; if still >=700ms, initiate 10% canary rollback to omega-v1.7
- 10:15–11:00 PT: expand canary per improvements, monitor, then finalize within 6 hours or revert changes if regressions occur

Attachments: p95_trend.png (chart), prod-logs-snippet.txt (tail traces). I'll assemble an evidence pack for the SLA team (evidence-pack.zip) and a short mutual action plan after we confirm scope.

Thanks — I can jump on a quick call if helpful.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-04T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected p95 increase — request for temporary tiered SLA exception for model omega-v2

Hannah — thanks for the quick triage and for drafting the plan. I agree with the proposed steps; a few operational clarifications and an internal approval to proceed:

Operational additions:
- Before rolling any traffic: pin FinTrade traffic to the dedicated GPU pool to avoid noisy neighbors during the window.
- Enable continuous KV-cache diagnostics and a short-lived debug log level for the affected variant (will expire automatically).
- Prepare a fallback policy: if error-rate rises >0.5% during canary, abort and rollback to prior stable variant immediately.

Approval: Internal ops authorizes a provisional 4-hour SLA carveout for diagnostics and an initial canary rollback to omega-v1.7 (10%) if p95 remains >=700ms after the 45-minute observation. If FinTrade approves a 6-hour window, we can extend monitoring and the rollback expansion cadence as Hannah proposed.

I'll prepare the short evidence pack (evidence-pack.zip) and a suggested client note you can send to Alex that explains what we will do and the acceptance criteria.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@fintrade.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintrade.com>
Date: 2028-11-04T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected p95 increase — request for temporary tiered SLA exception for model omega-v2

Hannah / Ben — thank you for the context and proposed plan. FinTrade is willing to approve a temporary SLA exception for up to 6 hours starting now to allow diagnostics and the controlled rollback you describe. A few points from our side:

- We accept the 45-minute evaluation period and the 10% canary rollback plan. If there's no material improvement within 45 minutes after the rollback starts, we consent to expand the rollback per your cadence.
- Please keep our procurement team and me updated on any potential billing/credit implications; Procurement (cc'd) will coordinate contract amendment if needed.
- We'd like a mutual action plan (short doc) and a JIRA ticket we can track. Also please provide the evidence pack once available.

Go ahead with your diagnostics and the KV-cache bump. Keep alerts configured to notify our SREs (we'll watch the dashboard).

— Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Engineering, FinTrade
alex.mercer@fintrade.com | +1 212-555-0124

Thanks Alex — we have your sign-off for the 6-hour exception. Actions we are taking now: 

1) 09:45–10:00 PT: KV-cache TTL increase and pinning long-sequence traffic to the dedicated pool (in progress).
2) 10:00 PT: evaluate 15m p95; if >=700ms we'll initiate 10% canary rollback to omega-v1.7.
3) If rollback required, we'll expand progressively and share per-step results in the JIRA: https://redwoodai.atlassian.net/browse/ENGINF-4921.

I've attached the preliminary evidence pack and charts (evidence-pack.zip, p95_trend.png). Procurement — I'll follow up with a short addendum to the contract for the exception window and any billing credits.

I'll post a short mutual action plan to the shared Drive link and ping your SRE channel with live dashboards. If anyone wants a bridge, I'm free for the next hour.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
